stories.headline: Estonia to close its Russia border crossings after attack on drone maker
body: Estonia will close its border crossings with Russia after an attempted arson attack on drone maker Threod Systems.
Eight people were detained overnight, and Tallinn says Russia's GRU military intelligence ordered the attack.
Russia called the move 'Russophobia'.
stories.vc: Attacks on defence suppliers raise security costs for Europe's fast-growing drone industry.

stories.headline: Africa CDC says Congo's Ebola outbreak is still not under control
body: Africa's top health agency says the Ebola outbreak in DR Congo is still not under control, six months on.
More than 11,200 cases and 5,500 deaths have been recorded since May 15.
Over 80% of new cases come from outside known contact lists.
stories.vc: Aid and vaccine funding gaps are making the outbreak harder and costlier to stop.

stories.headline: Iran says it targeted a US radar in Bahrain again
body: Iran's Revolutionary Guard says it sent six drones at a US air defence radar at Bahrain's Riffa Air Base.
Sirens sounded and Bahrain told residents to take shelter; it says its air defences stopped several attacks.
It is the second such claim in three days.
stories.vc: Gulf attacks keep oil shipping and insurance costs high.

stories.headline: SoftBank sells ₹1,885 crore of Meesho shares
body: SoftBank sold 7.6 crore Meesho shares in a block deal at ₹246.75 each.
The price was a 4% discount to Friday's close.
Fidelity bought the biggest chunk; Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley and Indian mutual funds also bought.
stories.joke: SoftBank books profit; Meesho's cart gets new owners.
stories.vc: Early investors cashing out after a stock rally is a normal sign of a healthy IPO market.

stories.headline: Air India's US flights go non-stop again, saving up to 5 hours
body: Air India has resumed non-stop flights to New York and Newark from Delhi and Mumbai.
Eased airspace limits mean no more fuel stop in Rome.
Total travel time falls from about 22 hours to about 17.
stories.joke: Rome wasn't built in a day, and now you don't have to stop there.
stories.vc: Shorter routes save fuel and crew costs on Air India's most valuable routes.

stories.headline: Goyal: Indian goods will get better US market access than rivals
body: Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal says the US has agreed that Indian goods will face lower duties than competitors' goods.
Both sides set a framework for the first phase of a trade deal in February.
Changing US tariffs have pushed back the signing.
stories.joke: Everyone wants a discount; India says it got one.
stories.vc: Lower tariffs would help exporters like textiles and electronics win US orders.

stories.headline: US Treasury chief wants an outsider to run Nvidia
body: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent says Nvidia should pick its next CEO from outside the company.
He gave the board 10 days to show it follows US export controls.
Jensen Huang quit on Thursday after an affair scandal. (The FT and Unhedged had no fresh piece today, so this is Al Jazeera's report.)
stories.joke: Job ad: must love chips, must not love drama.
stories.vc: Washington pressure on the CEO pick adds risk for the world's key AI chip maker.

stories.headline: Is bad news for Jensen Huang bad news for AI?
body: TechCrunch's Equity podcast asks what Huang's exit means for the AI economy.
The hosts note Nvidia had no succession plan and Huang was its biggest shareholder.
They wonder what happens to Nvidia's many startup investments. (Axios Pro Rata had nothing checkable, so this is TechCrunch's take.)
stories.joke: Plan B is a lovely thing to have before you need it.
stories.vc: Nvidia is a big investor in AI startups, so changes at the top could slow funding.

stories.headline: China's robotaxi firms plan for life with fewer Nvidia chips
body: Pony.ai's CFO says demand for AI chips already far outstrips supply.
If US export rules get stricter after Huang's exit, the company will train models on mid-tier hardware.
Nvidia is a key supplier to self-driving firms worldwide.
stories.joke: Necessity is the mother of efficiency.
stories.vc: Chip limits could push Chinese AV firms toward local suppliers.

stories.headline: Roblox CEO: AI means anyone can now make a game
body: Ben Thompson interviews Roblox CEO David Baszucki for the third time.
Baszucki says AI has changed what Roblox can do, now that literally anyone can build a game.
Roblox wants to be the 'Aggregator' that helps players find games; they also discuss ads.
stories.joke: Finally, a game where the boss level is the recommendation algorithm.
stories.vc: If AI floods the market with games, the money moves to whoever controls discovery.

stories.headline: Norwest raises $4B, its biggest fund, to back AI
body: Norwest, backed only by Wells Fargo, has raised a $4 billion fund, its 18th and largest.
It will invest in the US, India and Israel.
Focus areas include physical AI, voice AI, AI for cybersecurity, and aerospace. (No fresh, checkable Economist piece today, so this is TechCrunch's report.)
stories.joke: Four billion reasons to take your AI pitch meeting.
stories.vc: More big funds mean more cash for Indian AI startups too.

stories.statLabel: of men aged 18–24 hold rigid views of manhood
stories.headline: Hundreds of Swiss men march against violence toward women
body: Hundreds of men rallied outside parliament in Bern against misogyny and violence toward women.
Organisers say men must push back against the online 'manosphere'.
A Swiss study found half of men aged 18 to 24 hold restrictive views of masculinity.
stories.vc: Online platforms face pressure to curb misogynistic content.

stories.headline: Hungary pledges to ratify Europe's treaty on violence against women
body: Hungary's PM Péter Magyar says his government will ratify the Istanbul Convention.
The treaty requires better protection, shelters, legal aid and counselling for women.
Human Rights Watch says it's a welcome, overdue step.
stories.vc: Funding for shelters and legal aid will be the real test of the pledge.

stories.headline: Women's commission seeks probe into MLA's alleged messages to woman Collector
body: The National Commission for Women has asked Tamil Nadu's police chief for a fair inquiry.
It concerns claims that Kallakurichi MLA C. Arul Vignesh sent obscene WhatsApp messages to District Collector J.E. Padmaja.
The NCW wants an action taken report in 7 days.
stories.vc: Safe workplaces matter for keeping women in senior government jobs.

stories.headline: Telangana sets June 2027 deadline for TIMS and Warangal hospitals
body: Telangana must finish its TIMS hospitals at Alwal and LB Nagar, the Warangal Super Speciality Hospital and NIMS expansion by June 2, 2027.
CM Revanth Reddy also set December 2027 for the new Osmania General Hospital.
He promised funds would be released immediately.
stories.joke: Deadlines: the most optimistic part of any building.
stories.vc: New public hospitals should ease the load on NIMS, where surgeries face delays.

stories.statLabel: state cover for a liver transplant
stories.headline: Tamil Nadu plans liver transplants from living donors at government hospitals
body: Tamil Nadu is planning living-donor liver transplants at government hospitals, Health Minister KG Arunraj said.
Today only private hospitals in the state do them.
Sholinganallur's government hospital may also get a new mother-and-newborn emergency care centre.
stories.joke: Good news for livers, and for wallets.
stories.vc: Public transplant services could cut costs for families; the state insurance covers up to ₹22 lakh.

stories.headline: West Bengal to hire 2,000 doctors and up to 10,000 nurses
body: West Bengal will hire doctors, nurses and other staff on contract for government hospitals, from rural clinics to medical colleges.
Regular hiring through the public service commission takes 18 months to two years.
Hospitals can start hiring right away.
stories.joke: Hiring at hospital speed, not paperwork speed.
stories.vc: More staff could let existing beds and wards run at full capacity.

stories.headline: Daily Mail boycotts F1 after the FIA bans its reporter
body: The Daily Mail is boycotting Formula 1 after the FIA revoked the accreditation of its correspondent Jonathan McEvoy.
The FIA said his column about Charles Leclerc failed professional standards.
The paper calls it an attack on press freedom and will stay away for the rest of the season.
stories.joke: The paper's new F1 coverage: a blank page.
stories.vc: Media coverage drives F1's sponsor value, so press rows are bad for business.
